import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_19/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_19/test_1.csv"
    target_output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_19/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load Source 0
    # Schema: ['ocd_prop_id', 'calaccess_prop_id', 'ccdc_prop_id', 'prop_name', 'ccdc_committee_id', 'calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name', 'committee_position']
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, dtype={
        'ocd_prop_id': str,
        'calaccess_prop_id': 'Int64',  # Use nullable integer dtype
        'ccdc_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'prop_name': str,
        'ccdc_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name': str,
        'committee_position': str
    })

    # Load Source 1
    # Schema: ['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name', 'calaccess_filing_id', 'date_received', 'contributor_lastname', 'contributor_firstname', 'contributor_city', 'contributor_state', 'contributor_zip', 'contributor_employer', 'contributor_occupation', 'contributor_is_self_employed', 'amount']
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, dtype={
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name': str,
        'calaccess_filing_id': 'Int64',
        'date_received': str,
        'contributor_lastname': str,
        'contributor_firstname': str,
        'contributor_city': str,
        'contributor_state': str,
        'contributor_zip': str,
        'contributor_employer': str,
        'contributor_occupation': str,
        'contributor_is_self_employed': bool,
        'amount': float
    })

    # Rename committee_name in df0 to committee_name_x to match target schema
    df0 = df0.rename(columns={'committee_name': 'committee_name_x'})

    # Rename committee_name in df1 to committee_name_y to match target schema
    df1 = df1.rename(columns={'committee_name': 'committee_name_y'})

    # Merge df0 and df1 on calaccess_committee_id
    # This join is necessary to combine committee info from source0 with contributor info from source1
    # Use inner join to keep only matching committees
    merged = pd.merge(
        df0,
        df1,
        how='inner',
        on='calaccess_committee_id',
        suffixes=('_x', '_y')
    )

    # Select and reorder columns to match target schema:
    # ['ocd_prop_id': string,
    #  'calaccess_prop_id': integer,
    #  'ccdc_prop_id': integer,
    #  'prop_name': string,
    #  'ccdc_committee_id': integer,
    #  'calaccess_committee_id': integer,
    #  'committee_name_x': string,
    #  'committee_position': string,
    #  'committee_name_y': string,
    #  'calaccess_filing_id': integer,
    #  'date_received': string,
    #  'contributor_lastname': string,
    #  'contributor_firstname': string,
    #  'contributor_city': string,
    #  'contributor_state': string,
    #  'contributor_zip': string,
    #  'contributor_employer': string,
    #  'contributor_occupation': string,
    #  'contributor_is_self_employed': boolean,
    #  'amount': float]

    target_columns = [
        'ocd_prop_id',
        'calaccess_prop_id',
        'ccdc_prop_id',
        'prop_name',
        'ccdc_committee_id',
        'calaccess_committee_id',
        'committee_name_x',
        'committee_position',
        'committee_name_y',
        'calaccess_filing_id',
        'date_received',
        'contributor_lastname',
        'contributor_firstname',
        'contributor_city',
        'contributor_state',
        'contributor_zip',
        'contributor_employer',
        'contributor_occupation',
        'contributor_is_self_employed',
        'amount'
    ]

    # Ensure all target columns exist in merged dataframe
    # If any columns are missing, fill with NaN or appropriate default
    for col in target_columns:
        if col not in merged.columns:
            merged[col] = pd.NA

    # Select columns in order
    result = merged[target_columns]

    # Convert dtypes to match target schema exactly
    # ocd_prop_id: string
    result['ocd_prop_id'] = result['ocd_prop_id'].astype(str)

    # calaccess_prop_id, ccdc_prop_id, ccdc_committee_id, calaccess_committee_id, calaccess_filing_id: integer (nullable)
    int_cols = ['calaccess_prop_id', 'ccdc_prop_id', 'ccdc_committee_id', 'calaccess_committee_id', 'calaccess_filing_id']
    for col in int_cols:
        result[col] = pd.to_numeric(result[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    # prop_name, committee_name_x, committee_position, committee_name_y, date_received,
    # contributor_lastname, contributor_firstname, contributor_city, contributor_state,
    # contributor_zip, contributor_employer, contributor_occupation: string
    str_cols = [
        'prop_name', 'committee_name_x', 'committee_position', 'committee_name_y', 'date_received',
        'contributor_lastname', 'contributor_firstname', 'contributor_city', 'contributor_state',
        'contributor_zip', 'contributor_employer', 'contributor_occupation'
    ]
    for col in str_cols:
        result[col] = result[col].astype(str).replace({'nan': pd.NA})

    # contributor_is_self_employed: boolean
    # The source dtype is bool, but after merge it might be object, so convert carefully
    # Convert to boolean with nullable boolean dtype
    result['contributor_is_self_employed'] = result['contributor_is_self_employed'].map(
        {True: True, False: False, 'True': True, 'False': False, pd.NA: pd.NA, None: pd.NA}
    ).astype('boolean')

    # amount: float
    result['amount'] = pd.to_numeric(result['amount'], errors='coerce').astype(float)

    # Write to CSV
    # Use index=False to avoid writing the index column
    result.to_csv(target_output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
